{{Quote|At the behest of Moff Landric of Emmo sector, the Imperial Office of Criminal Investigation has assigned a Special Enforcement Officer to bring the art thief known only as the Tombat to justice.|TriNebulon News|<ref name="GNN-SWAJ8" />}}
The '''Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations (IOCI)''', was the primary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agency]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Led by a [[Director/Legends|director]], the IOCI was responsible for investigating and fighting criminal activities, specifically those of criminal syndicates and individuals who committed crimes on multiple [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. IOCI also managed the [[Imperial Enforcement DataCore/Legends|Imperial Enforcement DataCore]], a database for posted [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]]. The IOCI was formed in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] from the [[Republic Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Republic Office of Criminal Investigations]], its predecessor under the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

The jurisdiction of the IOCI included most of the known [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. As such they frequently worked with local law enforcement agencies, [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]], and various branches of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]. They also worked with the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]], the Empire's secret police. However, the ISB focused more on political investigations while the IOCI strictly focused on the enforcement of criminal law. Alongside the regular [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] and [[Detective/Legends|investigators]] in its employ, the IOCI had two elite operatives. The first were the [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]], an apolitical police force in existence since the early days of the Republic, and the [[Special Enforcement Officer/Legends|Special Enforcement Officers]], most who were recruited from the Sector Rangers and conducted undercover operations.

==Overview==
{{Quote|When the decision came down to get the IOCI involved in the Tombat case we didn't have much trouble in finding the right officer for the job.|IOCI Director Jacen Corbit|<ref name="GNN-SWAJ8" />}}
The Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations served as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] primary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agency]]. The IOCI was notoriously apolitical and focused strictly on criminal law enforcement in contrast to its secret police counterpart, the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] (ISB), which focused on political investigations. The IOCI investigated crimes that occurred in multiple jurisdictions as well as organized crime and criminal syndicates.<ref name="SW:LEotECR" /> It also supervised the activities of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] such as managing the [[Imperial Enforcement DataCore/Legends|Imperial Enforcement DataCore]], which listed all current [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]]. When a person wanted someone caught, they paid the full bounty to the IOCI which would extract a fee and then post the bounty on the Enforcement DataCore.<ref name="CSWE:IOoCI">{{CSWECite|II|93|Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations}}</ref> The IOCI would also issue [[Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate/Legends|Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificates]] (IPKC), allowing persons to conduct bounty hunting activities and to use lethal force if necessary.<ref name="CSWE:IPKC">{{CSWECite|II|94|Imperial Peace Keeping Certificate}}</ref>

Led by a [[Director/Legends|director]], the IOCI employed [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] and [[Detective/Legends|investigators]] in its service. In addition to them, the IOCI also had two elite operatives, the [[Sector Ranger/Legends|Sector Rangers]] and the [[Special Enforcement Officer/Legends|Special Enforcement Officers]]. The Sector Rangers were one of the oldest police forces in existence. They were mostly assigned to provide law enforcement services in the farthest stretches of Imperial space and generally worked in pairs or teams. Rangers were authorized to deputize who ever they needed to fulfill their tasks and could commander local police resources or [[Militia/Legends|militias]] if need be. The Special Enforcement Officers (SEO) were mostly recruited from the Sector Rangers. They often conducted highly dangerous or undercover missions and were fiercely independent generally working alone. Both the Sector Rangers and the SEOs were given a large latitude in enforcing the law. As they generally focused on larger targets, petty crimes were often overlooked and their cavalier attitude and willingness to work with pretty much anyone made them popular among the populace, though not necessarily COMPNOR and the ISB.<ref name="SW:LEotECR" />

==History==
{{Quote|I will not rest until the Tombat is brought before an Imperial court to answer for his crimes!|IOCI Inspector Zanza Gata|<ref name="GNN-SWAJ8" />}}
Under the [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]], the [[Republic Office of Criminal Investigations/Legends|Republic Office of Criminal Investigations]] served as the primary criminal investigations service during the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. With the [[Declaration of a New Order|formation]] of the Empire in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], it became the Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations. Placed under the banner of The Galactic Empire, the IOCI continued as it had before with little change, save its name.<ref name="CSWE:ROoCI" />

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], the IOCI posted bounties on the Enforcement DataCore for former [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. The posting of bounties for former members of the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] was a first in history.<ref name="GNN-SWAJ4">{{JournalCite|4|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref> That same year at the behest of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Landric]], the IOCI assigned [[Inspector/Legends|Inspector]] [[Zanza Gata]], a Special Enforcement Officer, to bring the art thief known only as the "[[Tanda Marelle|Tombat]]" to justice. IOCI Director [[Jacen Corbit]] introduced the SEO to a packed room of reporters in a dramatic press conference on [[Danteel]]. Gata made a brief statement promising to fully investigate the crimes and bring the thief before a court. It was also at that time, the [[TriNebulon News/Legends|TriNebulon News]] reporter, [[Andor Javin]], reported to the IOCI his theory that the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] was the long sought after criminal known as [[Cynabar]]. However, the IOCI took little notice of his theory.<ref name="GNN-SWAJ8" />

[[Mulvek Gra]] was an IOCI [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] stationed on the planet [[Celanon/Legends|Celanon]]. He was too old for field duty, but had served previously with [[System Sub-Commander]] [[Jared Brojtal]] and was like an uncle to his son. When the boy was killed during the [[Bombing of Syndaar Military Prep School]], he vowed to assist Jared in any way possible to locate [[Ort Hoogra-D'En]], the [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] responsible. Mulvek kept an eye on a group of persons who accepted the bounty on Ort, and fed the leads they discovered back to Jared.<ref name="GtG-ND">{{WEGCite|story=Gone To Ground|book=No Disintegrations (West End Games)}}</ref>

[[Jerik Snivas]] served as an investigator for the IOCI for many years. He was eventually promoted to an important position in the local office on [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Kwenn Space Station]]. However, years of shady dealings led him to leave IOCI to avoid being investigated and prosecuted. He became a free-lance expediter where his connections allowed him to stay in business.<ref name="ST-ND">{{WEGCite|story=Seregar Turnabout|book=No Disintegrations (West End Games)}}</ref>

After the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the IOCI remained relatively intact but only in those areas under staunch Imperial control. Other Imperial factions operated offices similar to the IOCI. However, the IOCI became increasingly fragmented as the Empire dissolved.<ref name="GG11:CO" />
